summary: Prioritize everyday biological mysteries and body sensations (pruned fingers, leaky eyes, pineapple burning) over general natural facts to capture high initial views.
Formulate hook sentences as direct contradictions or shocking revelations that immediately flip an assumption in the viewer's mind.
Keep titles punchy and use high-contrast emoji pairings to boost curiosity without relying on complex phrasing.
Eliminate long setup phrases or throat-clearing context in the first sentence; start right at the point of conflict.
Target a high stayed percentage above 60% by making the hook directly challenge a common physical sensation everyone experiences.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
avoid: Starting hooks with descriptive background information or boring definitions.
Using long, academic introductions that give the answer away before the viewer is hooked.
Writing passive first sentences that fail to create an immediate sense of intrigue or conflict.
next_experiment: Test an A/B split where Video A uses a direct bodily sensation contradiction ('You think you know why you sweat...') and Video B uses an external nature fact ('This tree makes poison...'), measuring which one achieves a stayed_pct above 60%.
